rubric.name: Sponsored video review
rubric.description: Would this brand approve this sponsored script as written?
rubric.context:
You review a creator's script for a sponsored video against the brand's brief. The brief lists the audience,
what the product does, and claims the brand must never make. Judge only the script text.

levels.label: off
levels.description: Aimed at people the brief doesn't target

levels.label: partial
levels.description: Some overlap with the brief's audience

levels.label: exact
levels.description: Speaks directly to the audience the brief describes, in their situation

criteria.name: Shows what the product actually does

levels.label: vague
levels.description: Praise without showing any feature from the brief

levels.label: some
levels.description: Mentions features, but tells more than it shows

levels.label: shown
levels.description: Shows the brief's features in use, with concrete results

anchors.missing: No clear sponsorship disclosure near the start
anchors.disclosed: The script says plainly, near the start, that the video is sponsored

criteria.name: No claim the brand can't make

anchors.unsafe: At least one claim is on the brief's must-not list or promises an outcome the brand can't guarantee
anchors.safe: Every claim is one the brand could legally make; nothing on the brief's must-not list

gates.message: Brand safety: the script makes a claim on the brand's must-not list

evidence.label: script.md
evidence.text:
# Small Desk Studio: "I tracked every dollar for 30 days"

[0:00] Last month I spent $214 on things I don't remember buying. So for 30 days I tracked every dollar.

[0:08] Quick note: this video is sponsored by Tallyleaf, the budgeting app I used for the whole month.

[0:14] Day one: I connected my cards and Tallyleaf sorted three months of spending into categories in about a minute.

[0:25] The first surprise was subscriptions. Four of them, $47 a month, and I'd forgotten two.

[0:36] Tallyleaf flags a subscription the day before it renews, so I cancelled the two I never open.

[0:48] Week two, I set a grocery budget with my roommate. We both see the same number, and it updates when either of us pays.

[1:10] By day 30 I'd spent $386 less than the month before. Not because of willpower; I just stopped being surprised.

[1:22] What I'd change: the charts are a bit small on my phone, and the web app is still in beta.

[1:30] If you want to try it, the link is in the description. First month free with code SMALLDESK.

[1:36] Next week: the $40 desk upgrade that fixed my back.
